newsitem.title: UK: Nat Grid pension ruling widely expected.
newsitem.headline: Nat Grid pension ruling widely expected.

text.p: A ruling by a British court on Tuesday in favour of electricity transmission company National Grid Group Plc and generator National Power Plc over their use of pension surpluses to fund redundancy payments had little impact on shares as it was largely expected, analysts said.
But they added there was some relief as the negative impact of an adverse ruling would have been greater.

"It seems common sense prevailed, as everyone expected. The worry was what would have happened to pension schemes in the UK if the companies had lost," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
Shares in National Power were down six pence after news of the ruling at 521.5 pence, after touching a low earlier of 517 pence, while National Grid was off a penny at 216 pence.
Mr Justice Robert Walker allowed an appeal by National Grid against a decision by Britain's pensions ombudsman that it should return 43 million stg.
He also ruled that the arrangements made by National Power had been valid and effective.
The judge said the ombudsman's decision had been based "on a misunderstanding of the terms of the scheme and of the employers' duties in dealing with the surplus."
But he said the two National Grid employees who brought the case would be able to appeal the ruling.
"The ruling was better news than had the companies lost," another analyst said.
